Gateway/proxy pattern + sidecar vs central proxy

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-05 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Jared Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Das (Redwood SE), Ethan Boyd (Conductor CTO), Lina Morales (Platform Engineer), Samir Patel (Security), Ravi Chandra (ML Eng)

Summary (auto): Conductor wants to understand integration effort for using Redwood for their internal orchestration layer. They run an edge gateway, several microservices using LangChain and an internal LlamaIndex-based ingest. Key concerns: auth, data residency, rate limits, and cost predictability.

00:00:05 Jared (AE): hey everyone, thanks for carving time. quick intros?
00:00:12 Ethan (CTO): yeah ethan here, i'm CTO at Conductor, we own the orchestration layer, mainly evaluating options to host LLM inference.
00:00:20 Lina (Platform): lina, platform eng, i'll own integration with our gateway and service mesh.
00:00:23 Jared: perfect, and i'm jared, AE at Redwood, with priya our solutions engineer.
00:00:28 Priya (SE): hi all. quick agenda: we'll cover deployment modes, SDKs/connectors, gateway patterns, rate limits, and observability hooks, then q+a and next steps.

00:01:10 Ethan: high level we have three constraints: 1) some requests include PII and must stay in our VPC, 2) real-time low latency on edge endpoints, 3) cost must be predictable for high-volume chat flows.
00:01:25 Priya: got it. to confirm - you currently run a central gateway that routes requests to internal microservices, and those services call LlamaIndex-backed retrieval + a generation step?
00:01:34 Lina: yeah exactly, we have a proxy that handles routing, auth, and throttling now. the LlamaIndex piece is in a separate retrieval service.

00:02:05 Jared: quick clarification on terms — Redwood Hosted means you hit our public API, Dedicated gives you reserved capacity (your own GPU pool) with consistent throughput, and Private is our VPC/on-prem option where control plane is customer-managed.
00:02:20 Ethan: can you run through integration patterns? we prefer not to change our gateway much.
00:02:27 Priya: absolutely. three patterns we've seen: 1) direct SDK calls from your service to Redwood API (fastest to implement); 2) a sidecar on each service that proxies calls and handles KV cache, batching, and auth; 3) a central inference proxy/gateway that aggregates requests — which sounds like your current approach. each has tradeoffs on latency vs batching efficiency.
00:02:55 Lina: sidecar seems nicer for local batching, but we worry about operational surface area.
00:03:01 Priya: yeah sidecars increase deploys, but help with prefix caching and low-latency for hot keys. central proxy simplifies ops but may add a network hop.

00:03:45 Samir (Security): on private hosting — real requirement is that any PII flows must not leave our VPC; can Redwood run the runtime inside our VPC and still keep the console hosted?
00:03:56 Jared: yes that's the Private model — control plane in Redwood but runtime in your VPC or on-prem. we can integrate with your KMS/HSM for key management, and retention policies are configurable.
00:04:10 Samir: what's the audit/logging surface? do you export per-token traces?
00:04:18 Priya: we provide per-request traces, token-breakdown for cost, and can stream audit logs to your S3/log pipeline. there are minor naming differences in the API but we can map fields.

00:05:05 Ravi (ML): on SDKs, we use a mixture: Python services call LangChain agents, our ingestion uses LlamaIndex, and some older services call a raw REST endpoint. how smooth is the SDK story?
00:05:20 Priya: Redwood SDKs have first-class LangChain integrations — an LLM wrapper that looks like any other provider. LlamaIndex connectors are community-maintained but we have a maintained example repo. our SDK also supports structured output and tool-calling patterns.
00:05:35 Ethan: are there any breaking changes we should watch for with model pinning and rollouts? we need deterministic responses for some workflows.
00:05:45 Jared: you can pin model versions at the route level, and we support canary rollouts. deterministic exact same output isn't guaranteed across model versions but you can lock a model and snapshot prompts for replay.

00:06:50 Lina: rate limits — we already enforce per-tenant quotas at the gateway. can Redwood enforce per-route or per-api-key quotas so we don't double-enforce?
00:07:02 Priya: yes, Redwood supports per-key and per-route quotas. You can define burst tokens, soft vs hard limits, and integrate with your own token bucket in the gateway. If you want, Redwood's proxy can expose X-RateLimit headers for easier coordination.
00:07:22 Lina: nice — does that integrate with our central RBAC? we use SAML SSO and service accounts.
00:07:30 Samir: plus we need SAML SSO and SCIM user provisioning.
00:07:35 Jared: we support SSO (SAML/OIDC) and SCIM provisioning on enterprise plans. For service-to-service auth we typically recommend API keys bound to a project with attached quotas.

00:08:40 Ethan: observability — we need traces correlated across our gateway and Redwood so we can see where latency comes from. is there an open tracing/span model?
00:08:52 Priya: yes, we emit trace IDs and propagate them if you pass an incoming trace header. we have a tracing hook that can emit OpenTelemetry spans, and per-token breakdowns show time spent in batching, kernel time, and network. sometimes the transcriber mashes that as 'kernel thyme' in notes.
00:09:15 Ravi: are the OpenTelemetry hooks available in Hosted or only Dedicated/Private?
00:09:20 Priya: Hosted includes basic tracing; Dedicated/Private gives deeper hooks and more retention/ingest endpoints.

00:10:10 Lina: about the gateway/proxy — if we keep our central proxy, what's a minimal change approach?
00:10:15 Priya: minimal: your proxy attaches an API key, forwards request bodies to Redwood, and proxies back. You can enable per-route model mapping at Redwood side so you don't have to change client code much. For batching, you can optionally add a small aggregator that groups small requests for higher throughput.
00:10:35 Ethan: what's the expected latency hit for that extra hop? we need sub-150ms p95 for short prompts.
00:10:42 Priya: depends on region and model. For small 64-token prompts on Dedicated we routinely see 60-120ms p95; adding a proxy hop typically adds 5-30ms in same VPC. If you go Hosted across public internet, that might add 20-80ms.

00:11:30 Samir: any red flags around data residency — we have EU customers and need data to stay in eu-west-1.
00:11:38 Jared: you can restrict routing policy by region; Hosted gives region options, Dedicated can be provisioned in eu-west-1, Private obviously runs in your VPC region. We'll include that in the security pack.

00:12:10 Ravi: LlamaIndex specifically — we've built a custom retriever that embeds docs and stores them in a self-hosted vector DB. can Redwood's pipeline call into that or do we need to push vectors?
00:12:25 Priya: two options: 1) keep retrieval local and send retrieved context with the prompt (we recommend this for PII); 2) use Redwood embeddings if you want managed vectors — that requires syncing. For your case, local retrieval + send context is simplest and keeps data in your VPC.
00:12:46 Lina: about embeddings, does Redwood's embedding pricing differ for Dedicated?
00:12:52 Jared: embedding units are meterable; Dedicated pricing tends to be more favorable at high volume, we can show a comparison in the sizing worksheet.

00:13:40 Ethan: security-wise, Samir will want SOC2 docs and an architecture diagram. Samir, any specific audit log granularity you need?
00:13:48 Samir: per-request user id, which model served, timestamp, and a token-level cost estimate is ideal. Also want to know retention defaults and ability to purge.
00:13:58 Priya: we can stream per-request metadata and token-cost estimates to your SIEM, and retention/purge policies are configurable on Private/Dedicated. Hosted has standard retention but enterprise plans can do custom windows.

00:15:05 Ravi: SDK friction — we have a Python LlamaIndex pipeline; if we swap provider to Redwood in LangChain, do we need to rewrite prompts?
00:15:15 Priya: no major rewrite; our LangChain wrapper conforms to the LLMPredictor interface. There are small differences in structured output handling but we have example notebooks showing the migration.

00:16:00 Lina: any examples of proxy sidecar configs? we use envoy sidecars.
00:16:08 Priya: yes we've got an envoy filter example that injects auth headers and propagates trace ids; we'll share the repo link.

00:17:00 Ethan: can you support canary rollouts—like 10% to Dedicated and fall back to Hosted if Dedicated saturates?
00:17:08 Jared: yes, Redwood's routing policies can do weighted routing by percentage and fallback chains for model variants or deployment modes. We also can do automatic fallback when capacity is reached.

00:18:15 Samir: question on quotas — if we set a hard quota per-tenant, will Redwood throttle server-side or return 429s and metric hooks?
00:18:26 Priya: we'll return 429s and emit quota events to your webhook or metrics endpoint. You can choose to have soft limits that warn vs hard enforcement.

00:19:10 Ravi: on the mini-benchmark — what telemetry do you need from our side? we can send 500 sample prompts with expected tokens and typical retrieval context sizes.
00:19:20 Priya: ideal: send sample prompts, average context length, embedding sizes, and expected concurrency. We'll instrument latency, p95/p50, token cost, and per-request traces.

00:20:05 Ethan: procurement timeline — we want a pilot in q4, pilot budget approved, procurement signs off in 6–8 weeks. any gating factors?
00:20:15 Jared: primary gates are security review and SSO/SCIM configuration. For Dedicated we also need capacity planning. We'll do a small pilot on Hosted or Dedicated depending on comfort — many teams start Hosted to validate integration then move to Dedicated for consistent economics.

00:21:40 Lina: a few quick nitty-gritty items: do you support signed URLs for audit exports? and can we rotate API keys programmatically?
00:21:51 Priya: yes we support signed export URLs to S3-compatible endpoints and key rotation via API + SCIM-managed service accounts for automation.

00:22:30 Ethan: pricing ask — can you send a simple model comparing Hosted per-token vs Dedicated commit for 10M tokens/month?
00:22:40 Jared: yes we'll attach a worksheet showing break-evens and conservative throughput assumptions.

00:23:55 Samir: threat model question — if we run Private in our VPC, what data is ever visible to Redwood?
00:24:02 Jared: with Private runtime in your VPC, Redwood's control plane has metadata for billing and monitoring but you can opt into minimal telemetry. We can do an air-gapped mode for on-prem where control plane access is limited.

00:25:30 Ravi: one small gotcha we hit with another vendor: embeddings drifted after a model update causing index mismatches. How do you handle model upgrades for embeddings?
00:25:42 Priya: we recommend versioned embedding models and an embedding migration path; Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization/model pairings and flag regressions with evals. You can pin embedding model versions used for indexing.

00:26:55 Lina: let's talk errors — when Redwood falls back, do we get structured reason codes so our gateway can decide to retry vs degrade gracefully?
00:27:05 Priya: yes we return structured error payloads with codes like FALLBACK_CAPACITY, RATE_LIMIT, AUTH_FAIL, etc. We can include recommended retry-after semantics.

00:28:20 Ethan: any sample code to wire LangChain with Redwood's SDK?
00:28:25 Priya: yes we have a gist and a sample repo; i'll drop links. the pattern is basically swapping the provider class.

00:29:45 Samir: compliance — we use third party auditors, will Redwood accommodate an ATO-style questionnaire?
00:29:53 Jared: we can provide standard security pack and work with your auditors; for Private we can do more detailed checks.

00:30:30 Ravi: curious about batching — in Dedicated, if we need very low latency for some routes but high throughput for others, can you set per-route batching windows?
00:30:42 Priya: yes batching policies are configurable per-route: you can set max latency window, min batch size, and a latency SLO preference. That lets you keep some routes low-latency and batch other bulk workloads.

00:31:50 Lina: is there a way to simulate cost impact of batching changes? our finance team wants worst-case vs best-case cost.
00:31:58 Jared: we'll include cost modeling in the worksheet; Redwood Optimize can run recommendations and show delta estimates for batching, cache hit rates, and quantization.

00:33:05 Ethan: okay wrap-up — what are the immediate next steps?
00:33:10 Jared: 1) send Dedicated sizing + pricing (Jared) 2) priya to run mini-benchmark with your sample prompts (Priya) 3) send SOC2 + topology (Jared) 4) schedule follow-up technical deep dive for sidecar/envoy example (Priya + Lina)

00:34:00 Lina: thanks, that timeframe works. we'll get samples to priya by Monday.
00:34:07 Ethan: procurement will expect a pilot contract; we'll loop in procurement after security review.

00:34:30 Priya: quick note — sometimes transcriptions say 'KV cash' instead of 'KV cache', so apologies if the auto notes are weird.
00:34:40 Jared: lols yes the transcripts do fun things.

00:35:00 Samir: small question — do you support IP allowlisting?
00:35:06 Jared: yes IP allowlists, VPC peering, and private endpoints are available on Dedicated and Private.

00:36:20 Ravi: performance tuning — any knobs for sequence length distribution optimization? we have chat with variable context.
00:36:30 Priya: runtime picks kernels based on observed seq length and we have quantization profiles for long-context models; batching heuristics can be tuned to group similar-length requests.

00:37:50 Ethan: thanks, this was helpful. we'll review and send the sample data.
00:37:58 Jared: great, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule. thanks all.

Action items recap (auto): Jared - pricing/sizing/workbook + SOC2/security pack; Priya - mini-benchmark and envoy example; Samir - supply audit constraints; Conductor - send sample prompts and concurrency estimates.

End of transcript.
